title: Moses Amyraut: all human acts, good, evil or indifferent, designated by decrees executed unfailingly, without violating freedom
source_text: XVII. Hic quoque viam singularem sequi videtur inclytae & celeberrimae memoriae vir Moses Amyraldus. Ille ergo quaecunque ab hominibus fiunt sive bona, sive mala, sive de eorum genere quae habentur indifferentia, aeternis Dei decretis designata, & praedefinita esse existimat, eaque decreta certissime & indeclinabiliter executioni mandari: sic tamen ut nec in eo violetur hominis libertas, nec Deus autor peccati statuatur.
pass_a_gloss: XVII. Here also that man of renowned and most celebrated memory Moses Amyraut seems to follow a singular way. He therefore thinks whatever things are done by men whether good, or evil, or of that kind which are held indifferent, to be designated and predefined by the eternal decrees of God, and those decrees to be put into execution most certainly and unswervingly: yet so that neither is the freedom of man violated in this, nor is God made author of sin.
pass_b_english: Moses Amyraut, a man of renowned and most celebrated memory, also seems to follow a way of his own here. He holds that whatever men do, whether good, evil, or of the kind counted indifferent, is designated and predefined by God's eternal decrees.
Those decrees, he holds, are carried out with complete certainty and without fail, yet in such a way that human freedom is not violated and God is not made the author of sin.
